Romanian Business News - ACTMedia :: Services | About us | Contact | RSS Home Daily Financial & banking Economic Companies Energy & Environment President Dan: We face the same threat on the eastern flank and in the Arctic region We face the same threat on the eastern flank and in the Arctic region, and behind this threat is the Russian Federation, President Nicusor Dan said on Monday before attending the European Arctic Summit in Finland. "We are an important country on the eastern flank and we face the same threat on the eastern flank and in the Arctic region. Of course, Russia is behind this threat. It includes drone [attacks], attacks on critical infrastructure, cyber attacks and acts of sabotage. As we face similar attacks, we need similar means of deterrence and preparedness to deal with them. That is why we are here," the head of state said. He brought to mind that Romania is part of the Helsinki Format and will host the next summit at the beginning of next year. He also said that Romania has expertise in the Black Sea in areas including mine clearance, intelligence gathering and undersea cables. "It is important to share our expertise with the countries on the eastern flank and with the countries bordering the Arctic. There are also interesting economic opportunities. In Romania, we have expertise in minerals, both their extraction and processing. There is cooperation between the Romanian and Finnish geological institutes on this matter and we also have expertise in shipbuilding. So this is a good framework for cooperation, to bring investment to the eastern flank and the Arctic region," Nicusor Dan added. European security is shared security, and what happens in one part of our continent has direct consequences for all of us, and nowhere is that clearer than along the continuum running from the Arctic through the Baltic to the Black Sea, Romania's President Nicusor Dan wrote on Monday in a social media post. "The European Union therefore has an strong role to play in strengthening defence readiness, resilience, infrastructure, economic security and connectivity across these regions. Romania supports enhanced military mobility linking the Black Sea to Northern Europe, as well as a structured Black Sea-Arctic dialogue to match this connectivity with a common strategic understanding." Dan went on to say that delivering on this requires strong EU-NATO cooperation, a coherent approach to trade and the environment, and close work with key partners such as the United States. "Romania is ready to assume its share of responsibility and to bring concrete added value to collective efforts," he said, adding that these priorities should be properly reflected in the forthcoming revised EU Arctic Strategy. Air power is one of the clearest expressions of European and NATO solidarity, from the Arctic to the Black Sea, Romania's President Nicusor Dan said on Monday after touring the Lapland Air Wing military base in Finland. The visit happened on the sidelines of the European Arctic Summit, with Dan saying that he saw what it means to guard NATO's northern edge every single day. "My thanks to the Finnish Air Force for the warm welcome and the professionalism on display. Rovaniemi and Romania's air bases stand at opposite ends of the same flank, but our paths are converging. This base is where Finland's F-35 capability begins. Romania is on the same journey, moving from the F-16 to the F-35 in the years ahead. We have a great deal to learn from one another ? on pilot training, on base infrastructure, on sustainment and on industrial production. Romania is ready to deepen this cooperation," Dan wrote in a social media post. He participated in the European Arctic Summit in Rovaniemi, Finland. Under Latvian law, prosecutors are expected to decide in the near future whether to bring charges. If charges are brought, there are three possible outcomes in cases of this type: the prosecutor’s office may impose a penalty itself; prosecutors may reach an agreement with the accused on an admission of guilt and punishment and ask a court to approve it; or the case may be sent to court for trial under the standard procedure. Amendments to the Criminal Law that entered into force in November 2022 introduced criminal liability for driving or teaching someone to drive a vehicle if an alcohol concentration exceeding 1.5‰ is detected in a breath or blood test. A vehicle is also confiscated if its owner was driving while heavily intoxicated or refused to undergo a test for the presence of intoxicating substances. If the vehicle driven under the influence belongs to another person, the offender may be ordered to pay the full or partial value of the vehicle. Latvia usually donates such confiscated vehicles to Ukraine’s defenders. Advertisement The Criminal Law provides for up to one year of imprisonment, probation supervision and a five-year driving ban for such an offence. As previously reported by LETA, Uzulnieks was caught driving with an alcohol level of 3.09‰ on the 12th of September. Municipal police stopped the driver of a Škoda in Stopiņi parish after he was found to be driving under the influence of alcohol. The State Police were called to the scene. The vehicle has been seized. Advertisement Uzulnieks is no longer a member of the Latvian Farmers’ Union (LZS), which is part of the Union of Greens and Farmers (ZZS). The party received a statement from Uzulnieks informing it that he was suspending his membership. Newsflash Newsroom , 05.10.2026, 21:28 Nomination – On Monday, Romania’s President Nicușor Dan nominated Luca Niculescu as the new prime minister following fresh consultations with all parliamentary political forces. Luca Niculescu (55) is a well-known figure in both diplomatic and media circles. A former journalist, editor-in-chief of RFI Romania, and host of foreign policy programs, Niculescu was appointed Romania’s ambassador to France in 2016, a post he held for six years. Since 2022, he has served as a State Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and as the national coordinator for Romania’s OECD accession process. Of all the parliamentary parties that attended the consultations, only the PSD put forward a nominee for prime minister, party leader Sorin Grindeanu. The third prime minister designate, the Liberal MEP Siegfried Mureșan, failed to secure the Parliament’s vote of confidence. Nobel – The first Nobel Prize awarded this year, the one for Medicine, went to American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for “their discoveries regarding light-activated ion channels and optogenetics.” Nobel Prizes, which also recognize outstanding achievements in physics, chemistry, literature, peace, and economics, come with a prize sum recently raised to 12 million Swedish crowns (equivalent to approximately 1.21 million US dollars) and bring winners instant fame, the kind unimaginable to the vast majority of scientists, according to international news agencies. The Nobel Prize was established by the wealthy Swedish chemist and entrepreneur Alfred Nobel, best known as the inventor of dynamite. In his will, he directed that the bulk of his fortune be used to fund “prizes awarded to those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.” Incident – Two people lost their lives and 11 were urgently evacuated by Romanian authorities after a Turkish grain-laden ship was struck by a drone in the Black Sea on Monday. According to the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs, Coast Guard vessels and a helicopter from the General Inspectorate of Aviation took part in the rescue operations. The incident occurred 20 nautical miles off the Romanian coast and 9 nautical miles from the Pescăruș oil platform, which is owned by a company in which the Romanian state, through the Energy Ministry, holds a minority stake. The ship, which sank, had departed from the Ukrainian port of Izmail. Letter – The ‘Friends of Cohesion’ group, comprising 17 EU member states, has sent a joint letter to Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, currently holding the rotating presidency of the Council of the Union, calling for agriculture and cohesion to remain central priorities in the next European budget cycle, announced the Romanian President Nicușor Dan. “First and foremost, we want an ambitious European Union budget; we want substantial funding for the cohesion and agriculture sectors, precisely to bridge the gaps between citizens of different European countries,” stated the Romanian head of state. Priorities – The European Parliament’s priorities for the EU multiannual budget, the approval of the new EU defense innovation program, tackling the cost-of-living crisis, and protecting patients against the health risks posed by counterfeit medicines are the main topics on the agenda of the European Parliament plenary session starting Monday evening in Strasbourg. On Tuesday, the European Parliament will be debating the situation in Ukraine and condemn the elections in Russia in a separate round of talks. The MEPs will look ahead to EU summit on October the 15th and 16th during a debate with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU. Ahead of the meeting of heads of state or government, the MEPs will discuss measures to boost Europe’s economic competitiveness, continued support for Ukraine in the face of Russia’s war of aggression, expectations for the 2028–2034 EU budget, and the situation in the Middle East. MEPs will also discuss, among other things, ways to make housing affordable, and, on Wednesday, the ongoing cost-of-living crisis. Olympiad – Romanian students won three gold and two silver medals at the 19 th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics, held in the Vietnamese capital, Hanoi. According to the Romanian Education Ministry, the Romanian team, comprising five students, made to the podium in all categories. The competition brought together over 310 contestants from 64 countries. SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENT – Between October 5 and 9, Radio Romania’s technical team is migrating the broadcasts of the public radio service’s stations to a new technical system. Consequently, we will be airing a backup broadcast via shortwave, across all languages ​​and frequencies used by Radio Romania International. In the meantime, you can find us online at www.rri.ro , including on-demand with updated programs and content, as well as on the RRI apps for Android and iOS and on our social media profiles. (LS)
